lessonRef.title: Skill consolidation: normal distributions, the empirical rule, and their limits

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 58 and standard deviation 7. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 37 and 79?
choices: about 50%
about 99.7%
about 68%
about 95%

items.prompt: A researcher runs an observational study of volunteers who chose their own group. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.

items.prompt: A random sample of 625 people gives a sample proportion of 33%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±4%, giving 29% to 37%
±8%, giving 25% to 41%
±33%, giving 0% to 66%

items.prompt: In 1000 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 38 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 3.8% of simulations, which is not unusual.
The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 3.8% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 116 and standard deviation 20. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 96 and 136?
choices: about 68%
about 50%
about 99.7%
about 95%

items.prompt: A researcher runs a sample survey with randomly selected participants. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.

items.prompt: A random sample of 2500 people gives a sample proportion of 42%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±42%, giving 0% to 84%
±2%, giving 40% to 44%
±0%, giving 42% to 42%
±4%, giving 38% to 46%

items.prompt: In 1000 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 21 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 2.1% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.
The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.
The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 2.1% of simulations, which is not unusual.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 114 and standard deviation 16. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 66 and 162?
choices: about 50%
about 95%

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A researcher runs a randomised controlled experiment with participants randomly assigned to treatments. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.

items.prompt: A random sample of 400 people gives a sample proportion of 67%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±5%, giving 62% to 72%
±67%, giving 0% to 134%
±10%, giving 57% to 77%

items.prompt: In 100 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 2 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 2% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.
The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 2% of simulations, which is not unusual.
